title: Can You See Your Piece in Progress? Workshop Updates & Pre-Shipment Photos | WRYDECO
meta_description: Can you see your custom solid wood furniture in progress? Learn how WRYDECO provides workshop progress updates, timber selection photos, and pre-shipment crating verification.
body_html:
Commissioning an heirloom solid wood furniture piece is an intimately personal experience. When you order an architectural bed frame or a sculptural branch bookcase, you are not merely purchasing manufactured inventory off a warehouse shelf; you are commissioning master artisans to shape living timber into a bespoke work of functional art. Naturally, discerning clients frequently ask: Can I see my piece in progress, and can I receive photographs before it ships?

WRYDECO welcomes client engagement throughout the crafting journey. Because each made-to-order piece undergoes approximately 15 to 20 business days of meticulous handcrafting by master artisans in Vietnam followed by 3 to 5 business days in transit (18 to 25 business days estimated total delivery window), we offer transparent milestone updates upon customer request. From raw hardwood slab selection and dry mortise assembly to final hand-rubbed oil finishing and pre-shipment crating, client transparency is woven directly into our artisan process.

How does WRYDECO share workshop progress photography during the crafting cycle?

Every WRYDECO creation begins when an order is finalized through our online storefront or bespoke design consultation. Unlike high-volume automated factories where automated assembly lines conceal production, our studio coordinates directly with artisan workshops in Vietnam to track individual pieces by client commission.

If you wish to follow your furniture piece as it takes shape, simply contact our support team at support@wrydeco.com after placing your order or note your request during checkout. Our online concierge coordinates with workshop craftspeople to capture authentic bench-side digital photographs at pivotal transformation stages. These images are delivered directly to your email inbox, giving you an intimate window into the hand-carving, joinery fitting, and oiling rituals that define true craft heritage.

[IMAGE: wrydeco_logo_39305860579418.jpg]

Follow these four recommendations when requesting workshop photo updates:

  • Request progress updates during checkout or email support@wrydeco.com within your first week of ordering.
  • Understand that workshop photos capture genuine bench craft in working studio lighting rather than studio glamour shots.
  • Review grain patterns and natural timber tones early in the carving cycle when timber slabs are shaped.
  • Communicate with your design specialist if you have specific custom sizing or finish requests.

Which specific crafting milestones can be documented upon customer request?

Handcrafting a major architectural furniture piece involves distinct artisanal milestones. While daily video feeds are not practical in active woodworking environments, WRYDECO documents three primary milestones for interested clients:

  1. Timber Selection & Milling: Master craftspeople inspect kiln-dried solid hardwood slabs, examining natural grain direction, growth rings, and live-edge contours. Photographing raw timber blanks gives you an early view of the unique organic figuring that will distinguish your finished piece.
  2. Dry Joinery & Structural Assembly: Once branches, limbs, or canopy arches are hand-carved, artisans perform a comprehensive "dry fit" on the workshop floor. Every mortise, tenon, and concealed steel sleeve is test-assembled without glue to verify precise alignment and structural balance.
  3. Oil Finishing & Natural Lustre: After fine hand-sanding with progressively finer grits, craftspeople hand-rub plant-based, zero-VOC hardwax oils deep into the timber pores. Milestone photos taken during finishing capture the breathtaking moment when the natural grain warms, deepens, and reveals its authentic color palette.

[IMAGE: wrydeco_logo_39305860612186_2fa155fa-6aa5-4b78-bf0e-03c11df99628.jpg]

Keep these four milestone guidelines in mind:

  • Timber selection photos showcase the natural wood grain and live-edge contours before cutting.
  • Dry fit assembly photos confirm proportional balance and joinery accuracy before final sanding.
  • Finishing photos demonstrate the deep color warmth achieved with zero-VOC hardwax oils.
  • Each documented milestone reassures you that genuine hand craftsmanship guides every step.

Why are pre-shipment inspection photographs critical before freight crating?

Before any completed furniture piece enters our crating department, it undergoes a rigorous final quality assurance audit. This pre-shipment inspection serves as a crucial quality gate for both our workshop and our clients.

During final inspection, our studio photographers document the fully finished piece from multiple angles under balanced studio lighting. We inspect all finished surfaces for smooth tactile feel, verify dimensions against client order specifications, confirm all pre-drilled mounting holes and hardware kits, and photograph the piece alongside its custom-built wooden freight crate. Sending these pre-shipment photographs to the client provides complete peace of mind that their commission has been executed flawlessly before it begins motor freight transit.

[IMAGE: wrydeco_logo_39305860907098.jpg]

Review these four pre-shipment verification standards:

  • Comprehensive multi-angle photographs confirm that your chosen finish matches order details.
  • Dimension checks ensure that custom width, depth, and height specifications align with your room plans.
  • Hardware pack verification confirms that all structural brackets and Allen keys are packed inside.
  • Crate inspection photos verify that internal foam cushioning and moisture barriers are secure before sealing.

How does the 15-20 business day crafting timeline progress from timber to final oil finish?

Understanding the workshop production rhythm allows clients to appreciate the dedicated care invested in their commission. Each piece follows a disciplined four-week progression:

  • Week 1 (Days 1–5): Timber acclimation and raw slab selection. Hardwood timber is inspected for grain integrity and moisture equilibrium. Initial dimensional milling establishes structural foundation members.
  • Week 2 (Days 6–10): Hand sculpting and architectural joinery. Artisans hand-carve organic branch contours using gouges and rasps. Internal steel alignment fittings are machined into joints.
  • Week 3 (Days 11–15): Dry fitting and progressive hand-sanding. The full structure is assembled on the workshop floor to verify balance and level perches, then hand-sanded across 120, 180, and 240 grits.
  • Week 4 (Days 16–20): Hand-rubbed hardwax oil finishing, 48-hour curing, pre-shipment photographic audit, and custom timber crating.
  • Transit (3–5 business days): International express freight transit to your regional delivery hub.

[IMAGE: wrydeco_logo_39305861234778.jpg]

Remember these four policy guidelines regarding your order:

  • Order cancellation or detail modification is 100% free within the first 6 hours after ordering (Golden Window).
  • Complimentary standard shipping is included on eligible orders worldwide; wall mounting or installation is not included.
  • Returns are accepted within 30 calendar days of delivery for damaged, defective, or incorrect items with store-paid shipping.
  • All pieces include a 1-year limited warranty against manufacturing defects in materials and craftsmanship.

  • Day 20: The piece is cushioned in high-density foam, secured in a custom-built plywood crate, and transferred to freight dispatch. Total estimated delivery window: 18 to 25 business days from order placement.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I request live video calls with the artisans in Vietnam?

Due to time zone differences and active workshop machinery noise, scheduled live video calls are not practical. However, our studio concierge regularly provides high-resolution digital photographs and recorded video clips of your piece at key crafting milestones upon request.

Is there an additional charge for receiving in-progress workshop photos?

No. WRYDECO provides complimentary workshop progress updates and pre-shipment photographs for clients who request them. It is part of our commitment to transparent artisanal craftsmanship.

Can I request modifications to my piece after seeing in-progress photos?

Minor surface adjustments (such as slight finish tone deepening) can often be accommodated before final oiling. However, core structural dimensions cannot be altered once timber milling begins after our 6-hour golden cancellation window.

What happens if I notice an issue in the pre-shipment photos?

If pre-shipment photos reveal an aesthetic detail that differs from your order confirmation, our craftspeople adjust it in the workshop before packing. This prevents transit delays and guarantees that the delivered piece matches your expectations.
